newsitem.title: INDIA: India expels Pakistani diplomat in kidnap row.
newsitem.headline: India expels Pakistani diplomat in kidnap row.

text.p: India said on Monday it had expelled a Pakistani diplomat as the two arch rivals traded charges of kidnapping one another's diplomats over the past two days.
India said it expelled the Pakistani diplomat "as he was involved in activities incompatible with his official status," a diplomatic euphemism for spying.
The Indian foreign ministry charged in a statement that a staff member of the Indian High Commission in Islamabad was kidnapped outside his home by 15 Pakistani intelligence agents on Monday.
It said it was in the wake of the expulsion of a Pakistani diplomat, identified by Indian officials as Nur Mohammad Mattoo.

The Pakistani High Commission said in a statement it had protested to the Indian foreign ministry after Indian intelligence agents abducted a Pakistani diplomat in Delhi on Saturday and kept him in illegal detention for 16 hours.
An Indian foreign ministry spokesman said Mattoo was the official Pakistan said was abducted.
"The Ministry of External Affairs has conveyed its most serious concern at this unacceptable action of the Pakistani agencies," the Indian foreign ministry said.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since their independence from British rule in 1947, two of them over the disputed region of Kashmir.
